title: Undo and Redo
drDigitalIntro:
Made a mistake? Undo it instantly — no retyping needed.
• Ctrl+Z (or Command+Z on a Mac) undoes your last action. Press it again to undo more steps.
• Ctrl+Y (or Ctrl+Shift+Z) redoes what you just undid — on a Mac, Command+Shift+Z.
• Undo works in almost every app: word processors, email, photos, drawing tools.
• Common mistake: deleting a lot of text and panicking — just press Ctrl+Z a few times to bring it back.
• You can undo many steps, not just the very last one.

playgroundTask.goal: Use Undo and Redo to fix a mistake

steps.say: Type a few words in the editor.
Press Ctrl+Z (or Command+Z) to undo what you just typed.
Press Ctrl+Shift+Z (or Command+Shift+Z) to redo and bring it back.

drDigitalSuccess: Ctrl+Z is the safety net under everything you type. Made a mess of something? Undo it and start that bit again.
drDigitalHint: Type something first, then use the Undo and Redo shortcuts. Hold Ctrl (or Command) and press Z to undo, or Shift+Z to redo.
